Worlds and World Coins — semantic diff

Branch feature/worlds-and-world-coinsBase 2cf090eHead 53ccaa3 Target mainDate 2026-11-18 Commits 9Files 47 · +3223 / −240 Written by REVIEW: · Claude Opus 5.5

Summary

The branch adds 13 worlds in three sizes, a new currency (world coins) earned per 500 trophies and from ten world-coin hack codes, a world screen before Play, Training and a room's start, saved progress v8 with a migration, two-tab merge rules, and a room protocol that keeps friends on the previous version in Canyon Small. Every Before | After was produced from the base (2cf090e) and the head, except the result line, which is manual.

  • Canyon Small is unchanged where it was promised: the same layout object (CANYON) and the same 3D geometry and colours (fingerprint identical; 431 → 21 meshes).
  • Old saves migrate and are paid once for the trophies they had (1240 → 500 world coins); new accounts start with 0; reset clears all five world fields.
  • Rooms: guests build the host's world from the start message; the server removes friends without a room version only outside Canyon Small, and the host is told who and why.
  • Two Should-fix findings: the same 500-step won in two stale tabs is paid twice, and the bot seek rule also finds players hiding in bushes (in Canyon Small too).
  • Checks: 8 pass · 1 n/a · 0 fail; tests: pytest 56 passed, Vitest 375 passed, svelte-check 0 errors.

Recommendation: Approve with follow-ups — no Blocking finding; fix the double payment in the two-tab merge (with a test) and decide whether bots may seek players hidden in bushes before or right after merging.

Spec context

.specs/features/2026_11_16_worlds_and_world_coins_spec.md — statements S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7, S8, S9, S10, S11, S12, S13, S14, S15, S16, S17, S18, S19, S20, S21, S22, S23, S24; Steps 1–8 (all ✅ Done), decisions D1–D12. Issue #24.

Semantic diff

Why: Every match and every Training session was played in the same arena, the same size. Players want to choose between several worlds, each in Small, Medium and Large, so matches feel different and bigger worlds mean more running. Three worlds are free in Small; the others and the bigger sizes are unlocked with a new currency, world coins, earned per 500 trophies or from special hack codes that each account can use again after 30 days.

Breaking: None for players on this version: v2–v7 saves migrate and get world coins for trophies already reached; Canyon Small plays exactly as before. Friends on the previous version can still join and play rooms in Canyon Small; when the host starts in any other world or size the server removes them with "update-the-game" (S7, by design). As with earlier versions, a v8 save is not read by the previous version of the game. · Checks: 8 pass · 1 n/a · 0 fail

## README.md — section "Worlds and world coins"### Worlds and world coinsEvery match and every Training session is played in a **world**. There are 13 worlds, and eachcomes in three sizes:| Size | Ground ||------|--------|| Small | 30 × 24, today's arena || Medium | 36 × 30, about 1.5 times the ground || Large | 42 × 34, about 2 times the ground |A bigger size has more cover (walls and bushes), so fighters walk further to meet. The rulesare the same in every world: fighters, match length, overtime, bots, Training dummies, Supersand rewards.- **Free** for every account, in Small: **Canyon**, **Jungle Ruins** and **Neon Docks**.- **To buy** with world coins: **Lava Forge**, **Sky Islands**, **Crystal Caves**, **Mini City**,  **Kata Jungle**, **Candy Factory**, **Robot Workshop**, **Pirate Cove**, **Moon Base** and  **Desert Oasis**.**World coins** (🌍, shown on Home next to the credits; a new account starts with 0):- **Earn:** each time the account's total trophies reach the next 500 (500, 1000, 1500…) for the  first time, it gets **250 world coins** at once, and the result screen shows it. Each 500 pays  only once, even if the total goes down and up again.- **Old saves** get the coins for every 500 their trophies had already reached (1240 trophies →  500 world coins), and keep everything else.- **Prices:**  | To get | World coins |  |--------|-------------|  | A locked world in Small | 500 |  | A locked world in Small + Medium | 750 |  | A locked world in Small + Medium + Large | 1000 |  | The next size of a world you have (Medium after Small, Large after Medium) | 250 |- Credits cannot buy worlds, the `INFINITY` hack gives no world coins, and `OPENSESAME` does not  unlock worlds or sizes. Worlds come only from world coins.**World-coin codes:** ten codes, five give 500 world coins and five give 1000. They are typed onthe Hack screen or scanned like the other codes; the codes themselves are listed in`server/src/hack_star_server/world_codes.py`, not here.| Question | Answer ||----------|--------|| How often | Once per account. The same code works again for that account 30 days after it was used || Before that | It is refused, with the date it works again || Other accounts | Each account on the device has its own 30 days || Where the dates are kept | In each account's saved progress on the device, not on the server, so clearing the browser's data lets a code be used early || Shown | The Hack screen lists the used world-coin codes with the date they work again || Reset | **Reset coins and trophies** (Settings) makes every code usable again at once; **Reset all hacks** does not touch them || Changing | The amounts, the 30 days and the codes are all in `world_codes.py` |**The world screen** is opened by **Play** and **Training** before the match, and by the host of aroom before **START**:- The balance is shown at the top, and each world has a card with its name (free worlds are  tagged **Free**).- Each card has three size buttons, **Small**, **Medium** and **Large**. An unlocked size shows ✔:  tap it to choose that world and size (the choice is kept for next time, and the chosen card is  highlighted). A size you can buy shows its price in 🌍: tap it and confirm. With too few world  coins the screen says how many more are needed. A size above the next one stays 🔒 until the  smaller one is unlocked.- The bar at the bottom shows the chosen world and size; **START** plays it.- In a room, the host's world is used for everyone, including friends who have not unlocked it.  A friend on the previous version of the game can join only a room that plays in Canyon Small.  In any other world the server removes that friend, and the host is told why; the friend needs  to update the game.## docs/architecture.md — lines mentioning worlds, world coins or world_codes (79)10:     Screens --> Game["game/<br/>rules: World, Match, Bots"]21: | Server | `server/` | Python 3.13, FastAPI, port 8180 | Game data: the fighter catalogue, hack codes and world-coin codes; rooms for playing with friends (with the host's world) |33: | `GET /api/hacks` | The hack codes (`hacks.py`) and the world-coin codes (`world_codes.py`, with `world_coins` and `reuse_days`), for the printable QR page |34: | `POST /api/hacks/redeem` `{"code"}` | The hack for a code (any case, spaces trimmed), or 404 "Unknown code"; Author Q&A

Do old saves keep everything, and can the trophy world coins be paid twice?
They keep everything and get the free worlds in Small with Canyon Small chosen. The migration pays 250 per 500-step already reached and stores worldSteps, so later matches only pay steps above it (S9, S20; 1240 trophies → 500 world coins).
Do today's matches in Canyon change?
No. arenaFor('canyon', 'small') returns CANYON itself, and a test pins Canyon's 3D build (triangles, positions, colours) to the previous one; only the bot seek rule after 6 s without seeing anybody is new in every world (D2, D5).
Can a player use a world-coin code again early?
Only by clearing the browser's data or resetting the account: the codes are checked by the server, but the "used" dates live in the account's saved progress (D10). The game has no server accounts; server-side tracking is a Deferred Item.
What does a friend on the previous version see?
In Canyon Small, nothing changes. Elsewhere the server sends the existing room-error message with the reason "update-the-game", which older games show as it is; the host's lobby says who had to leave and why (D11).

6 · Bigger size wins, refund for a world bought twice

ui/src/lib/accounts.ts:243-277 · 48c67b5 · Step 2 · S13, S19 · D7

243/**
244 * A key whose number grew in this tab keeps the larger of both tabs; one that went down or was
245 * removed (a reset) keeps this tab's value.
246 */
247function mergeLargest<T extends string | numberGeneric constraint — A type parameter limited to some types. One helper merges both the code dates (numbers) and the sizes (strings), each with its own order function.>(
248 base: Record<string, T>,
249 local: Record<string, T>,
250 remote: Record<string, T>,
251 order: (value: T) => number,
252): Record<string, T> {
253 const merged = { ...remote }
254 for (const key of new Set([...Object.keys(base), ...Object.keys(local)])) {
255 const hadBase = Object.hasOwnObject.hasOwn — True only for an object's own key, never for one inherited from its prototype. A key missing from one tab means a reset or a code never used; a world id like 'constructor' cannot match by accident.(base, key)
256 const hasLocal = Object.hasOwn(local, key)
257 if (hadBase === hasLocal && same(base[key], local[key])) continue
258 if (!hasLocal) delete merged[key]
259 else if (hadBase && order(local[key]) < order(base[key])) merged[key] = local[key]
260 else if (!Object.hasOwn(remote, key) || order(local[key]) > order(remote[key])) merged[key] = local[key]
261 }
262 return merged
263}
264
265/** World coins this tab paid for a world that the other tab had already bought. */
266function worldRefund(base: Progress['worlds'], local: Progress['worlds'], remote: Progress['worlds']): number {
267 let refund = 0
268 for (const [id, localSize] of Object.entries(local)) {
269 const baseSize = base[id] ?? null
270 const remoteSize = remote[id] ?? null
271 if (worldCost(baseSize, localSize)Refund by cost difference — What this tab paid minus what the other tab's purchase already covers. Buying Small here and Small + Medium there ends with Medium and exactly 750 paid. === 0 || worldCost(baseSize, remoteSize) === 0) continue
272 const bigger = remoteSize !== null && worldCost(localSize, remoteSize) > 0 ? remoteSize : localSize
273 refund += Math.max(0, worldCost(baseSize, localSize) - worldCost(remoteSize, bigger))
274 }
275 return refund
276}
277

What changed: mergeLargest keeps the larger value per key unless this tab lowered or removed it (a reset); worldRefund gives back what this tab paid for a world the other tab had bought too. Why it matters: without the refund a world bought in two tabs would cost twice (S13). Check: the same idea is missing for worldSteps (finding 1).

What is good: Canyon's look is pinned by a geometry and colour fingerprint while the draw calls drop from 431 meshes to 21; the merge already refunds a world bought in both tabs; the server ignores every message of a removed socket except a new create or join; world prices, amounts and codes each live in one place; every new text exists in all five languages; and the Steps' tests cover each world × size (layouts, dummies, overtime, bots-only Large matches).

Not covered

  • Smoothness of Large worlds on a real iPad and phone (S23) and the camera QR scan — not measurable here; the Deferred Item points to the device-testing spec. Screenshots use software WebGL.
  • A real previous-version game in a room: simulated with a WebSocket member without version.
  • The reset warning text does not name world coins — already a Deferred Item of the spec.
  • The spec file itself (Part 2 logs) and .specs/spec-nx.json (model tiers; block kit-models, not part of the spec).
  • No lock files, dependencies, renames or generated files changed.

Concepts glossary

$state rune
Svelte 5's $state makes a variable reactive.
Array.reduce
Folds an array into one value.
Default parameter
A parameter that takes a value when the caller leaves it out.
Delta merge
Adds this tab's change (local − base) to the other tab's value instead of overwriting it.
Epoch milliseconds
Date.now() counts milliseconds since 1970 in UTC.
Filter before sort
Array.filter returns a new array, so the seats in the room state are not reordered or changed.
Generic constraint
A type parameter limited to some types.
Integer steps
Math.floor of total / 500 counts the 500-steps already reached.
Intl date formatting
Formats a date for a locale.
List comprehension
Builds a list from another in one expression.
Max merge
Keeps the larger of two counters.
Membership after removal
A removed seat is no longer in the room's list, while its socket stays open.
Migration chain
Each old version is lifted one version at a time until it is the current one.
model_dump
Pydantic's model_dump turns a model into a dict; exclude_none drops fields that are None.
Object.fromEntries
Builds an object from [key, value] pairs.
Object.hasOwn
True only for an object's own key, never for one inherited from its prototype.
Optional field (None default)
A field declared `int | None = None` is None when the message leaves it out.
Optional parameter
A parameter that may be left out (undefined).
Optional Pydantic field
A field with a default is optional in the model and in the OpenAPI schema.
Paid-steps watermark
A counter of what was already paid, compared with what is reached now.
Pick utility type
Pick<T, K> keeps only the listed keys of a type.
Pydantic strict mode
In strict mode Pydantic refuses values that would need a conversion.
Refund by cost difference
What this tab paid minus what the other tab's purchase already covers.
requestAnimationFrame
Runs a function before the next paint.
Store update
A Svelte store's update(fn) computes the next value from the current one.
Straight-line steering
The bot moves along the vector to its target, sliding along walls by the world's collision.
Ternary filter
One condition chooses between two skip rules.
Three-way merge
Compares what this tab started from (base), what it has now (local) and what another tab saved (remote).
Type guard
A function returning `value is T` narrows the type where it returns true.
unknown type
TypeScript's unknown forces a check before a value is used.
